notes: Breadboard coordinates are estimated from the circuit image. Bank 't' (rows a-e) is the half nearest the bottom rails in the picture, and bank 'b' (rows f-j) is the half nearest the top.
The bottom rail pair is taken as 'bn' (minus, black line) and 'bp' (plus, red line). Rail hole numbers are approximate.

The button straddles the centre gap with legs in columns 4 and 6. I assumed the catalogue pushbutton's port 1 is the column-4 pair (1.l=4b.f, 1.r=4t.e) and port 2 is the column-6 pair. That gives the schematic's topology: 5V reaches the switch through the orange wire, and the other side goes to pin 2 and the resistor.
The 10k resistor is a pull-down, from column 6 (bank t, row c) to column 9. A short black wire carries column 9 to the GND rail.
Pin 2 connects to the button through the teal wire at 6b.i, which is the same column-6 pair as the button leg and resistor.
The manual does not say which GND pin is used. I used GND.2 (the second GND in the power header), as the picture shows.
The Arduino sketch (Debounce) is software only and is not part of the graph.
